hook.line: Tomás has made up his mind about the café, and nothing his friends or Altamira say will change it. Spanish can shut every objection at once by saying the same verb twice.
hook.es: Digas lo que digas, voy a ir.

examples.es: Digas lo que digas, voy a ir.
examples.en: Whatever you say, I'm going. (to a friend)

examples.es: Insistas lo que insistas, no lo voy a hacer.
examples.en: However much you insist, I'm not going to do it. (to a friend)

examples.es: Hagas lo que hagas, no le digas nada.
examples.en: Whatever you do, don't say anything to her. (to a friend)

examples.es: Diga lo que diga Altamira, no vamos a vender el café.
examples.en: Whatever Altamira says, we're not selling the café.

examples.es: Vayas donde vayas, siempre hay un tinto.
examples.en: Wherever you go, there's always a tinto. (to a friend)

examples.es: Vengas cuando vengas, Simón tiene algo que decir.
examples.en: Whenever you come, Simón has something to say. (to a friend)

rule:
To say "no matter what", repeat the verb in its *que* form with a small word between: 

*Digas lo que digas*: whatever you say
*Vayas donde vayas*: wherever you go
*Vengas cuando vengas*: whenever you come
*Insistas lo que insistas*: however much you insist

Both verbs are the same verb, the same person, in the *que* form (*dices* becomes *digas*). Then comes the main sentence, ordinary and certain: *voy a ir*.

It is not a guess. The speaker has already decided.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a reduplicated subjunctive concessive.

readAndPick.es: Digas lo que digas, voy a ir.
options: Whatever you say, I'm going.
I'm going because you say so.
Whatever you said, I went.

readAndPick.es: Insistas lo que insistas, no lo voy a hacer.
options: If you insist, I'll do it.
However much you insist, I'm not going to do it.
You insisted, so I'm not doing it.

readAndPick.es: Hagas lo que hagas, no le digas nada.
options: Whatever you did, you told her nothing.
Whatever you do, tell her everything.
Whatever you do, don't say anything to her.

readAndPick.es: Diga lo que diga Altamira, no vamos a vender el café.
options: Whatever Altamira says, we're not selling the café.
Altamira says we're not selling the café.
Whatever Altamira said, we sold the café.

readAndPick.es: Vayas donde vayas, siempre hay un tinto.
options: I'm going wherever you go, with a tinto.
Wherever you went, there was a tinto.
Wherever you go, there's always a tinto.

readAndPick.es: Vengas cuando vengas, Simón tiene algo que decir.
options: When you came, Simón had something to say.
Whenever you come, Simón has something to say.
Simón will say something when you come.

readAndPick.es: Digan lo que digan, nosotros seguimos.
options: Whatever they say, we carry on.
Whatever you say, they carry on.
Whatever they said, we carried on.

readAndPick.es: Pase lo que pase, el café no se vende.
options: What happens is that the café isn't sold.
Whatever happened, the café wasn't sold.
Whatever happens, the café isn't for sale.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *digas* or *dices*, then type the whole sentence: ___ lo que ___, voy a ir. (Whatever you say, I'm going. To a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Digas lo que digas, voy a ir.
yourTurn.why: "No matter what" always uses the *que* form, *digas*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *insistas* or *insistes*, then type the whole sentence: ___ lo que ___, no lo voy a hacer. (However much you insist, to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Insistas lo que insistas, no lo voy a hacer.
yourTurn.why: Both verbs take the same *que* form: *insistas*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: Whatever you do, don't say anything to her. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Hagas lo que hagas, no le digas nada.
yourTurn.why: *Hagas lo que hagas* opens, then a negative command with *digas*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: Whatever Altamira says, we're not selling the café.
yourTurn.answer: Diga lo que diga Altamira, no vamos a vender el café.
accept: Diga Altamira lo que diga, no vamos a vender el café.
yourTurn.why: Altamira is one company, so the verb is *diga*, twice.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: Wherever you go, there's always a tinto. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Vayas donde vayas, siempre hay un tinto.
yourTurn.why: For places, use *donde* between the two verbs.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it *they* who talk and *we* who go: Whatever they say, we're going.
yourTurn.answer: Digan lo que digan, vamos a ir.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: Whenever you come, Simón has something to say. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Vengas cuando vengas, Simón tiene algo que decir.
yourTurn.why: For time, use *cuando* between the two verbs.

pitfalls.wrong: Dices lo que dices, voy a ir.
pitfalls.right: Digas lo que digas, voy a ir.
pitfalls.why: Almost. "No matter what" needs the *que* form, not the ordinary *dices*.

pitfalls.wrong: Digas lo que dices, voy a ir.
pitfalls.right: Digas lo que digas, voy a ir.
pitfalls.why: Both halves must match: the same verb, the same *que* form, twice.

pitfalls.wrong: Hagas lo que hagas, no le dices nada.
pitfalls.right: Hagas lo que hagas, no le digas nada.
pitfalls.why: A negative command also takes the *que* form: *no digas*.

personal: Think of something you have decided and will not change. Say it with *Digas lo que digas,…* or *Pase lo que pase,…*
